$comment: Theme palettes for the card face and desk surface (SPEC §5.3). A build input like data/deck.v1.json, not a shipped resource: F8 generates from it. Every pair listed in `contrast` is checked by scripts/check_theme_contrast.py, which is a gate, not a promise — the design handoff asked for a contrast table and nobody had run one, so both themes shipped colours that failed it.

thresholds.$comment: WCAG 2.2 AA. Body text 4.5:1, large text and meaningful non-text 3:1.

note-card.provenance: Ported from reference/valuescardsort.jsx. ACCENT corrected by D10 — the reference's #C75146 fails at 4.47:1 white-on, 4.35:1 on paper and 2.78:1 on felt.
note-card.$appearanceNote: The card carries its own stock and its own desk, so no pair below involves a system background and every ratio is identical in dark mode. A physical index card on a felt desk looks the same whichever way the room is lit.
note-card.$decorativeNote: The ruled lines of an index card carry no information. WCAG 1.4.11 scopes to graphics needed to understand content or identify a control; these are neither, so they are exempt by the criterion's own scope rather than by waiver.

mucha.provenance: Colour sourced from the mothballed Mucha-Design-System token set (Marty's own, primitive.color.json + semantic.light/dark.json). Desk REMAPPED — that system's bg.canvas/bg.surface-1 are document elevation steps at 1.12:1, which renders an almost-invisible card. Desk chosen by Marty 2026-08-31: violet.900. Dark variant dropped — see $appearanceNote.
mucha.$appearanceNote: Appearance-independent, like Note Card, and for the same reason: the card carries its own stock and its own desk, so no pair involves a system background. A dark variant was attempted and abandoned on evidence — the source system's dark layer inverts a document canvas, which puts a dark card on a dark desk at 1.25:1. Separating from a near-black desk needs a LIGHT stock, and a light stock needs DARK ink, which is the light palette. No card stock in the ramp satisfies both constraints (best was umber.500 at 3.26:1 stock/desk but only 4.35:1 ink/stock, under 4.5). Paper is light; a card in a dark room is still a light card.
